stories.headline: Two Helicopters Collide Over Rio de Janeiro, Killing All 6 Aboard; American Singer Oliver Tree Listed as Passenger
stories.summary:
Two helicopters collided in midair over Rio de Janeiro on Sunday morning and crashed in the city's western zone, killing all six people aboard, according to Rio de Janeiro's Military Fire Department. One of the helicopters came down in the parking lot of a car dealership, igniting a fire among electric vehicles on the lot before it was extinguished. Authorities said an investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collision.

Police confirmed that American singer and comedian Oliver Tree was listed on the passenger manifest submitted to aviation authorities, though officials said they had not yet been able to identify the bodies of those killed. Tree had performed in Buenos Aires on June 4 and posted a video on Instagram on Saturday showing him in a Brazilian neighborhood. Argentine streaming channel Blender confirmed that popular content creator Gaspar Prim Díaz, known as Gaspi, who had more than 2.8 million YouTube followers, was also aboard one of the helicopters.

An eyewitness at the scene, tire repair worker Fernandes de Freitas, said he saw one helicopter in flames after the midair collision and observed a passenger jump from the other aircraft before it struck the ground. The crash drew emergency responders to the western zone of the city, one of Brazil's largest metropolitan areas. Official identification of victims remained ongoing as of Sunday.

stories.headline: Anti-G7 Protesters Clash with Police in Geneva Ahead of Monday Summit Opening
stories.summary:
Protesters clashed with police in Geneva on Sunday ahead of the G7 summit set to begin Monday in Évian-les-Bains, France. Authorities deployed tear gas and a water cannon after demonstrators smashed windows and set a car on fire during a large anti-summit demonstration. The gathering drew protesters opposed to what they described as economic and political domination by the world's wealthiest nations.

The G7 summit will bring together the leaders of the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Canada, Italy, Japan, and the European Union beginning June 15. The meeting is expected to address a range of pressing global issues including the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, the Strait of Hormuz situation, and broader geopolitical tensions. One protester told reporters the core message was opposition to "all these countries that oppress us through money and power," though they expressed disappointment that the demonstration turned violent.

The unrest in Geneva serves as a prelude to what is expected to be one of the most diplomatically charged G7 summits in recent years. Previously covered reporting has noted that President Trump is expected to meet with Middle Eastern leaders on the sidelines, and French President Macron has planned a dinner at Versailles, with discussions around demining the Strait of Hormuz also on the agenda.

stories.headline: Vance Says He Will Weigh 2028 Presidential Run After November Midterms
stories.summary:
Vice President JD Vance said Sunday he plans to sit down with his wife Usha after the 2026 midterm elections to discuss next steps for his political career, including a potential 2028 presidential run. Speaking on CBS Sunday Morning in conjunction with the release of his new memoir, "Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith," Vance said he tries not to make decisions until he "absolutely must" but added he has "no doubt" that President Trump would support him.

Vance's comments mark the most direct public acknowledgment to date that a presidential campaign is under active consideration. The memoir, which details his conversion to Catholicism, has given him a high-profile platform to expand his public profile beyond his vice presidential duties. Speculation about a 2028 bid has grown steadily as Vance has become one of the most prominent figures in the Trump administration.

The vice president's remarks come as Republicans look ahead to a post-Trump political landscape. Vance, a former Ohio senator who became a close Trump ally after a well-publicized ideological evolution, would likely face a competitive primary field. No formal campaign apparatus has been announced.

stories.headline: Skydiving Plane Crash Kills All 12 Aboard Near Butler, Missouri
stories.summary:
A single-engine turboprop plane carrying a pilot and 11 passengers on a skydiving outing crashed shortly after takeoff from Butler Memorial Airport in Butler, Missouri, on Sunday morning, killing everyone aboard. The plane, a Pacific Aerospace 750XL operated by Skydive Kansas City, went down in a field around 11:30 a.m. and was engulfed in flames. Some of the victims' family members witnessed the crash, according to Bates County Sheriff Chad Anderson.

Acting airport manager Dennis Jacobs said the plane had just taken off and made a left turn before going down, and suggested the aircraft may have lost power and stalled while the pilot attempted an emergency landing on a nearby highway. Emergency responders extinguished the fire and searched the area beneath the flight path but found no one who may have attempted to jump before impact. Clergy and volunteers were dispatched to assist families at the scene.

The Federal Aviation Administration had personnel on scene Sunday afternoon, and a National Transportation Safety Board team was en route to investigate the cause. The Pacific Aerospace 750XL is a model widely used in skydiving operations as well as cargo, aerial survey, and medical evacuation flights. The crash is among the deadliest general aviation accidents in the United States in recent years.

stories.headline: Sen. Mitch McConnell Hospitalized; Condition Not Disclosed
stories.summary:
Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, 84, was admitted to a hospital Sunday morning, according to a statement from his senior adviser David Popp. The statement said only that McConnell 'is receiving excellent care' and did not provide a reason for the hospitalization or identify the facility.

McConnell, the longest-serving Senate Republican leader in U.S. history, has experienced a series of health episodes in recent years, including a fall in February 2025 that preceded his announcement that he would retire from the Senate at the end of his current term. He has also previously suffered a concussion from a fall in 2023, during which he was seen freezing mid-speech at public events, sparking widespread concern about his health.

McConnell remains a sitting senator from Kentucky and has continued to play a role in Senate affairs despite his announced retirement. No further details on his condition or expected length of hospitalization were available as of Sunday.

stories.headline: Trump Conditions FISA Renewal on Passage of SAVE America Voting Bill
stories.summary:
President Trump declared Sunday that he will not support renewing Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act unless Congress attaches his SAVE America Act, a sweeping voting overhaul measure, to the legislation. The announcement came via Truth Social posts as Section 702, one of the government's most powerful surveillance authorities, has already lapsed following a congressional deadlock.

Section 702 permits U.S. intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets overseas without a warrant, including when those communications involve Americans. It has long been opposed by civil liberties advocates on the left and libertarian-leaning conservatives on the right, while national security officials across administrations have called it indispensable. The SAVE America Act, by contrast, is a Republican-backed elections bill that Democrats have strongly opposed.

Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia criticized Congress broadly for allowing the authority to lapse, noting the timing coincides with the World Cup and the nation's 250th anniversary celebrations. Sen. Mark Warner, the lead Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said intelligence community leaders have told him they are 'terrified' of the current intelligence leadership situation, as Trump's nomination of Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence remains unresolved. The linkage of FISA to unrelated voting legislation sets up a significant confrontation in Congress with national security implications.

stories.headline: Update: Israeli Strike on Beirut Threatens U.S.-Iran Peace Deal as Trump Urges Restraint
stories.summary:
Israel carried out an air strike on Dahieh, the southern suburbs of Beirut and a Hezbollah stronghold, killing at least three people and wounding 15 others. The Israeli military said the attack targeted a Hezbollah command center after the group launched aerial targets toward northern Israel. The strike came just as the United States announced an agreement with Iran was close to being signed, throwing the broader diplomatic effort into uncertainty.

President Trump broke publicly with Israel over the timing, posting that the attack 'should not have happened particularly on a special day when we are so close to a Peace Deal with Iran,' while also insisting Israel has the right to defend itself. He said the Hezbollah provocation that triggered the strike was 'very small and meaningless' and called on all parties to halt attacks. Iran's chief nuclear negotiator accused the U.S. of failing to honor its commitments by not restraining Israel.

Israeli officials have expressed deep reservations about the emerging U.S.-Iran framework. An Israeli military official described the deal as 'very bad' and 'catastrophic,' while a defense official said none of Israel's stated war objectives were addressed in the agreement. Israel has maintained that military operations against Hezbollah must continue regardless of any U.S.-Iran arrangement, a position Tehran rejects, insisting any truce must include an end to the Lebanon conflict.

The strike opens the possibility of further escalation: Iran has vowed to respond to attacks on Beirut by striking Israel. Lebanon's government has separately sought to distance itself from Iran's influence and weaken Hezbollah domestically. The episode underscores the fragility of the U.S.-led diplomatic effort and the degree to which Israeli military operations could derail a deal the White House has described as imminent.

stories.headline: Nara Organics Recalls Baby Formula Nationwide After Infant Botulism Outbreak Across Three States
stories.summary:
Nara Organics has recalled its Whole Milk Organic Powdered infant formula sold nationally at Target stores and on its website after three infants in California, Pennsylvania, and Washington became ill with botulism between April and May. The babies, aged 2 to 5 months, were hospitalized and treated with BabyBIG, the FDA-approved intravenous medication derived from blood plasma of people immunized against botulism. The recall was announced Saturday following coordination between the FDA and CDC.

Infant botulism is a rare but serious condition caused when babies ingest bacterial spores that produce a toxin in the gut; immature gut microbiomes in infants under one year make them uniquely vulnerable. Symptoms include constipation, poor feeding, drooping eyelids, weak muscle tone, and difficulty swallowing or breathing. The FDA stressed that Nara Organics represents less than 1 percent of all infant formula sold in the United States and that no shortage is expected.

The CDC urged any caregiver with the formula to stop using it immediately, photograph the can, record the lot number and use-by date, label it 'DO NOT USE,' and store it away from other items for at least one month before discarding. The formula is manufactured in Europe but sold exclusively in the U.S. Parents whose infants show any symptoms were advised to seek immediate medical attention.

stories.headline: Georgia Special Session Called to Fix Looming Election Law Crisis Before July 1 Deadline
stories.summary:
Georgia lawmakers are returning to the state Capitol this week for a special session called by Republican Governor Brian Kemp, with one central task: resolving an election administration crisis created by a 2024 law that bans the use of QR codes for official vote tabulation after July 1, 2026 — a deadline now weeks away with no replacement system in place. The state's entire voting infrastructure relies on the barcode system, and neither the legislature nor the secretary of state's office has implemented an alternative in the two years since the ban was enacted.

The secretary of state's office and the State Election Board have compounded the problem by issuing conflicting guidance to county election officials, raising the prospect of widespread confusion and litigation after the deadline passes. A special U.S. House election is already scheduled for July, meaning the dysfunction could affect a federal race. Lawmakers may opt to extend the QR code deadline to give themselves more time rather than rushing a new system into law.

The QR code controversy has roots in the post-2020 election period, when former President Trump and his allies falsely claimed Georgia's touchscreen voting machines had switched or deleted votes. Republican legislators passed the 2024 ban partly in response to those concerns, as well as from election integrity advocates who argued voters cannot verify their choices because QR codes are not human-readable. Trump's first executive order on elections targeted the same machines used in Georgia and more than a dozen other states, though courts have blocked that order.

The special session also includes redistricting work for the 2028 congressional maps. The QR code fix represents a rare case where a legislature must undo the consequences of its own prior action under a hard deadline, with a competitive midterm election cycle approaching.

stories.headline: Mexico Enacts Law Allowing Election Results to Be Voided Over Foreign Influence
stories.summary:
Mexico's Congress has approved a constitutional amendment, backed by President Claudia Sheinbaum's ruling Morena party, that would allow the government to void election results if it determines that foreign interference affected the outcome. The change raises significant concerns among democracy advocates and opposition figures, who warn it could be used as a political tool to nullify unfavorable results under the pretext of foreign meddling.

Critics argue the law's language is broad enough to give the governing party substantial discretion in determining what constitutes impermissible foreign influence, potentially undermining the independence of electoral institutions. Mexico has been engaged in ongoing trade and sovereignty tensions with the United States, and the amendment comes as the country navigates complex diplomatic pressures from its northern neighbor during USMCA renegotiations. Supporters of the measure contend it is a necessary safeguard for national sovereignty.

The reform is among the most consequential changes to Mexico's electoral framework in years, and its passage signals Morena's continued consolidation of political power following its landslide 2024 electoral victories. International observers and opposition parties are expected to scrutinize how and whether the provision is invoked in future elections.

stories.headline: Violence Mars NYC Knicks Championship Celebrations: Teen Shot, Buses Torched Near Times Square
stories.summary:
Chaotic scenes erupted in New York City early Sunday morning as jubilant celebrations over the Knicks' first NBA championship since 1973 turned violent in Midtown Manhattan. A 17-year-old was shot in the foot near 42nd Street and Broadway around 2 a.m., and five yellow school buses — which had been transporting World Cup fans — were set ablaze or destroyed with bats. Ten police officers were injured, including one struck by a glass bottle and another punched in the face.

The NYPD reported 63 arrests on charges including assault on a police officer, criminal possession of a weapon, criminal mischief, and resisting arrest. Additional incidents included four slashings or stabbings, destruction of private vehicles, and crowds refusing to disperse. Three people of interest were taken into custody and a firearm recovered from the scene near Times Square.

Knicks owner James Dolan had appealed for restraint immediately after the team's 94–90 Game 5 victory over the San Antonio Spurs in Texas, urging fans to 'be safe' and 'don't hurt anybody.' The violence unfolded as New York City is simultaneously hosting World Cup matches, compounding crowd management challenges for authorities. No fatalities were reported.

stories.headline: Trump Turns 80 With UFC Cage Fights on the White House South Lawn
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump marked his 80th birthday Sunday with an unprecedented spectacle: a professional UFC mixed martial arts event staged on the South Lawn of the White House, branded UFC Freedom 250. More than 4,000 attendees including Cabinet members, Republican lawmakers, and senior administration officials filled a temporary arena beneath a large metal arch fitted with lighting and video screens, with thousands more watching on big screens at the nearby Ellipse. Seven fights were scheduled to run past midnight.

Trump framed the event as part of broader celebrations of the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, though the evening was widely seen as a personal birthday celebration. UFC chief Dana White, a close Trump ally, called it 'a one of one event.' The White House held an official media walkthrough of the South Lawn in advance, and weigh-ins were held Friday night at the Lincoln Memorial.

The celebration came against a backdrop of significant political pressures. Trump is navigating an ongoing war with Iran, with a potential deal still being negotiated ahead of next week's G7 summit. Separately, a federal court this week ordered Trump's name removed from the Kennedy Center, and crews were seen removing the signage approximately a mile from the birthday festivities. The juxtaposition of the lavish White House event with those developments drew considerable media attention.

stories.headline: Collins Takes Aim at Platner's 'Angry Rhetoric' as Maine Senate Race Shapes Up as Cycle's Most Watched Contest
stories.summary:
Republican Sen. Susan Collins gave her first major national interview since announcing her 2026 re-election bid, telling Fox News Digital she is taking Democratic nominee Graham Platner seriously despite his mounting controversies. Collins, who has cast a record 10,000 consecutive Senate votes and chairs the Appropriations Committee, said she was surprised Gov. Janet Mills — whom she expected to be her opponent — dropped out of the primary. Platner won the Democratic nomination despite allegations including a tattoo recognized as a Nazi symbol, sexting with other women shortly after his marriage, and a denied allegation that he locked an ex-girlfriend in a room.

Collins framed the race as a contrast between her record of bipartisan work and what she called Platner's 'angry rhetoric.' In his primary victory speech, Platner accused Collins of being 'spineless and corrupt,' and has attacked her for her Iraq War authorization vote and support for parts of Trump's agenda. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has identified Collins' seat as a top Democratic target for the cycle.

The race has become a flashpoint in a broader debate about Democratic Party standards. As reported separately, national Democrats including Sen. Tina Smith have backed Platner, with Smith arguing that 'Democrats want to win' and that voters want candidates who speak to their concerns — a posture some in the party view as abandoning earlier commitments to candidate conduct standards established during the #MeToo era. Republicans argue the embrace of Platner reveals a double standard in how Democrats treat misconduct allegations.

stories.headline: UK and Japan Announce £18 Billion Investment Deal as Starmer Hosts Takaichi in London
stories.summary:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced an £18 billion bilateral investment agreement Sunday during talks in London. Under the deal, Japanese firms have committed more than £9 billion to UK infrastructure and financial services and up to £9 billion to offshore wind energy development, with Downing Street saying the package will create tens of thousands of jobs. Major Japanese companies including Mitsubishi Estate, Mitsui Fudosan, and Nomura Real Estate are among those committing funds over the next five years.

The two leaders also reaffirmed their joint commitment to the GCAP next-generation fighter jet program, which also involves Italy. A separate agreement was announced between Rolls-Royce and Japan's Atomic Energy Agency to develop next-generation nuclear technologies, and a broader technology partnership linking UK research and software expertise with Japanese manufacturing was also confirmed.

The deal comes as the UK economy faces headwinds. The IMF has warned that the ongoing U.S.-Israel war with Iran will hit the UK harder than any other advanced economy, and the Bank of England has cautioned that inflation could rise toward 6 percent in a worst-case scenario. UK GDP grew 0.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026 but analysts expect sluggish growth ahead. Conservative shadow business secretary Andrew Griffith said his party welcomed investment deals but criticized Labour's 'tax hikes and employer red tape' as undermining job creation.

stories.headline: UK Royal Marines Board Russian Shadow-Fleet Tanker in English Channel in First Operation of Its Kind
stories.summary:
British Royal Marine Commandos and National Crime Agency officers boarded a sanctioned oil tanker, the Smyrtos, in UK territorial waters in the English Channel on Sunday in the first UK-led interdiction operation targeting Russia's shadow fleet. The six-hour operation was supported by Royal Navy warships, military helicopters, and an RAF P-8 maritime patrol aircraft.

The shadow fleet refers to a network of vessels used to transport Russian oil in circumvention of Western sanctions imposed following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine. The Smyrtos had been operating under sanctions, and Sunday's boarding marks a significant escalation in the physical enforcement of those measures by a NATO ally.

The operation signals a shift from financial and diplomatic pressure to direct maritime interdiction as Western nations seek to tighten the economic squeeze on Russia. The move is likely to draw attention at the G7 summit opening Monday in Evian-les-Bains, France, where allied coordination on Ukraine and sanctions enforcement is expected to be a central agenda item.

stories.headline: Update: Trump to Meet Mideast Leaders at G7 as Macron Plans Versailles Dinner; Hormuz Demining Discussed
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump will attend the G7 summit opening Monday in the French lakeside town of Evian-les-Bains, with an unusually dense schedule of bilateral meetings focused on winding down the U.S.-Iran conflict. Senior administration officials said Trump plans to discuss demining operations in the Strait of Hormuz with allies, as confidence grows that a deal is near; Britain and France have expressed interest in assisting once hostilities pause.

Trump will hold separate meetings on the summit sidelines with the leaders of Egypt, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates — none of which are G7 members but were invited by French President Emmanuel Macron — as well as India's prime minister. The meetings reflect the extent to which the Iran conflict and its economic ripple effects are dominating an agenda that formally covers supply chains, critical minerals, immigration, and artificial intelligence.

Macron's office announced Trump will also attend a dinner Wednesday at the Palace of Versailles, framed as a commemoration of the 250th anniversary of American independence and described as a symbol of historic Franco-American friendship. The diplomatic pageantry underscores European efforts to maintain close ties with Washington as the Iran situation and NATO commitments remain in flux.

stories.headline: Norwegian Crown Princess's Son Faces Verdict Monday on 40 Charges Including Rape, as Mother's Health Deteriorates
stories.summary:
Marius Borg Høiby, 29-year-old son of Norwegian Crown Princess Mette-Marit, will receive a verdict Monday from three judges at Oslo District Court on 40 charges including four counts of rape. Prosecutors are seeking a sentence of seven years and seven months; defense lawyers have argued for one and a half years. Høiby, who has been in custody since February, will appear via video link for unspecified health reasons.

The case has drawn intense public attention in Norway, compounded by the simultaneous health crisis of his mother, who was placed on a lung transplant list last week. Doctors have indicated that patients placed on the list are typically considered to have approximately one year to live. An appeal court last week denied Høiby's request to be released to be with his ailing mother.

Høiby admits to lesser charges involving drugs and traffic offenses but denies the most serious allegations. The trial has also cast scrutiny on Crown Princess Mette-Marit over revelations of a three-year friendship with the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, generating what observers described as profound public sympathy for her health situation alongside unresolved questions about the future of the Norwegian royal family.

stories.headline: Update: Somali Referee Denied Entry to U.S. for World Cup Will Receive Full FIFA Tournament Fee
stories.summary:
FIFA has committed to paying Somali referee Omar Artan his full World Cup fee despite his being barred from entering the United States, sources told BBC Sport. Artan, the 2025 Confederation of African Football men's referee of the year, was interrogated for 11 hours by U.S. immigration authorities at Miami International Airport before being deported to Turkey and then flown home to Mogadishu.

A U.S. government official said Artan was denied entry due to an alleged association with suspected members of terrorist organizations. Artan said border officials questioned him about links to the Somali militant group Al-Shabaab, which he denied, stating he had the correct visa and travel documents and was simply a referee pursuing a lifelong dream.

The episode has added to broader criticism of U.S. visa and travel restrictions around the World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting. In a development reflecting his standing in the sport, Artan has since been invited to officiate the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg on August 12, and has vowed to qualify for the 2030 World Cup. The story has received wide international coverage across nine outlets and intersects with ongoing debates about immigration enforcement and the United States' image as a World Cup host.

stories.headline: Update: U.S.-Iran War Enters Critical Phase as Hormuz Blockade Holds and G7 Summit Looms
stories.summary:
The United States-Iran conflict continues to dominate global attention, with President Trump declaring a U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz after Iran seized two cargo ships in the waterway. More than 50 Iranian military bases have been damaged by U.S.-Israeli strikes since the war began in late February, according to satellite imagery analysis. Iran has struck American assets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain in retaliation, with Bahrain reporting damage to its capital overnight.

Diplomats on both sides continue to signal a deal is within reach, though Tehran has called reports of a finalized agreement 'speculative.' U.S. officials say any deal would require the destruction of Iran's enriched uranium, with details still being negotiated. Trump warned Iran 'will have to pay the price' for delays, while Iran's foreign minister said a settlement remains close.

Trump will head to the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains, France, beginning Monday, where he is expected to discuss demining the Strait of Hormuz with allies. Britain and France have expressed interest in assisting with the demining operation once a ceasefire is in place. Trump will also hold separate meetings with the leaders of Egypt, Qatar, the UAE, and India on the sidelines, and will dine with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Palace of Versailles on Wednesday to mark the 250th anniversary of American independence.

Energy markets have experienced wild swings since the conflict began, though U.S. shale production has partially insulated the American economy from the worst oil price shocks. The Strait of Hormuz blockade poses severe risks to global shipping and oil supply, with analysts watching closely for any movement toward a formal ceasefire agreement ahead of the G7 meetings.

stories.headline: New York Knicks Win First NBA Championship Since 1973, Defeat San Antonio Spurs in Five Games
stories.summary:
The New York Knicks clinched their first NBA title in more than 50 years on Saturday night, defeating the San Antonio Spurs 94-90 in Game 5 of the Finals in San Antonio. The victory ends a championship drought dating back to 1973 for one of the league's most storied franchises and its most prominent market.

The win capped a remarkable Finals run for the Knicks, who had already recorded the largest comeback in NBA Finals history earlier in the series and led 3-1 before closing out the title on the road. Fans who traveled to San Antonio for the clinching game described the moment as a once-in-a-generation celebration for a franchise and fan base long accustomed to disappointment.

The championship carries significant national profile given New York's media market and the Knicks' long-suffering fan base. The title is expected to generate substantial economic and cultural impact in New York City, where celebrations are anticipated in the coming days.

stories.headline: Democratic Party's Nomination of Scandal-Plagued Maine Candidate Raises Questions About Party Standards
stories.summary:
Maine Democrats have nominated Graham Platner as their U.S. Senate candidate despite a string of controversies, including a tattoo identified as a Nazi symbol, sexting with women shortly after his marriage, and allegations — which Platner denies — that he locked an ex-girlfriend in a room and forcefully twisted her arm. Platner cruised to the Democratic primary after Governor Janet Mills suspended her own campaign. He will face Republican Senator Susan Collins in November.

The nomination reflects a broader shift within the Democratic Party, which is increasingly prioritizing electoral viability over what it once regarded as disqualifying personal conduct. Senior Democrats including Minnesota Sen. Tina Smith have publicly backed Platner, arguing the party must focus on candidates who can energize voters and help Democrats regain congressional majorities lost in 2024. 'Democrats want to win,' Smith said.

Critics within and outside the party argue the embrace of Platner signals an abandonment of standards Democrats championed during the #MeToo era, when they pressured members including Sen. Al Franken to resign over allegations of unwanted touching. Supporters counter that the political landscape has changed and that Republicans have long tolerated similar or worse conduct among their own candidates without electoral consequences.

The Platner nomination is one of several recent cases testing the boundaries of Democratic tolerance, including Virginia's election of Jay Jones as attorney general after he sent a text suggesting the then-House speaker should be shot. The debate is shaping up as a central fault line heading into the midterm elections.

stories.headline: Haiti's Top Police Official and Family Kidnapped in Port-au-Prince
stories.summary:
Armed men in Haiti have kidnapped James Boyard, chief of staff to the defense minister and inspector general of Haiti's national police, in what officials and analysts describe as the highest-profile abduction of a government official in the country in recent years. Boyard's wife and six-year-old daughter were also seized during the Thursday incident in Port-au-Prince. A ransom has been demanded, according to the New York Times.

Boyard was a central figure in efforts to rebuild Haiti's armed forces under Defense Minister Mario Andrésol, who was appointed in March. Analysts with the International Crisis Group say gangs have been expanding kidnapping operations into areas of Port-au-Prince previously considered safe, and are increasingly targeting public officials either for higher ransoms or to deter government security operations against gang-held territory.

The abduction underscores the continued deterioration of security conditions in Haiti despite an international police mission deployed to assist local authorities. The United Nations reported earlier this month that gang violence has killed at least 2,310 people and caused 99 kidnappings so far in 2026, with nearly 1.5 million Haitians displaced from their homes — a record level.
